$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for RRCF per-category mandatory fields and the self-description contract. conformance/schema/rrcf-declaration.schema.json is GENERATED from this file by conformance/tools/gen_schema.py — edit this file, then regenerate. Field IDs and units follow the vocabulary already used by the reference controller (reference-implementation/RCSP1_UniversalRobotControl.jsx) so that profiles and reference implementation cannot drift apart.

selfDescriptionContract.statement: A generic controller, dashboard, or VLA MUST be able to render and interpret every declared telemetry field using only the declaration — no per-robot code, no out-of-band documentation, no vendor lookup table. A field that cannot be rendered from its own declaration is non-conformant, even if the field is present on the wire.
selfDescriptionContract.rationale: This is what makes one controller work against any robot. The moment a consumer needs to know that this vendor's 'soc' means battery percent, the operator layer has stopped being portable and RRCF has no reason to exist.
rules: unit MUST be a non-empty string for number, integer, and vector3 fields. Dimensionless ratios use '1'; percentages use '%'.
min MUST be strictly less than max.
warn_below and warn_above, when present, MUST fall inside [min, max].
enum fields MUST enumerate every value they can emit, in the values attribute, space-separated.
A field ID MUST be unique within a declaration.
A declared field MUST be published on the wire. Declaring a field the robot never emits is a conformance failure, checked at runtime, not at declaration time.
frequency_hz on a field overrides the telemetry endpoint rate for that field. Either the field or the endpoint MUST establish a rate.

universal.$comment: Applies to every category, including custom.

safety.notes: estop MUST declare required='true' and a topic. watchdog MUST declare timeout_ms and action.

command.notes: twist is additionally required for any category declaring locomotion axes — see categories[].requiresTwist. It is NOT universal: a fixed manipulator has no mobile base, and RRCA MUST NOT assume mobile-base Twist semantics for every category (architecture/rrca.md).

telemetry.purpose: The robot's own latched e-stop state. Distinct from the operator's last commanded estop value — an operator must be able to see that the robot actually stopped, not merely that a stop was sent.

The explicit runtime state RRCA is already required to report (architecture/rrca.md, RRCA core responsibility 9). Standardized value set, because the state machine is defined by RRCF itself rather than by the vendor.

manipulator.label: Fixed Manipulator (Arm)
manipulator.$comment: No mobile base: no locomotion axes, no mandatory twist, and no mandatory battery — a fixed arm is typically mains powered.

industrial_vehicle.label: Industrial Vehicle
industrial_vehicle.$comment: Typically engine powered rather than battery powered, so battery is not mandatory.

custom.label: Custom (vendor-defined)
custom.$comment: An open category cannot have a mandatory morphology vocabulary imposed on it. It still owes the universal set and the full self-description contract on every field it does declare — that is what keeps custom robots renderable by a generic controller.
